dataset.name: CROCUS Forward Scatter Disdrometer Data at Argonne National Laboratory Prairie Site
description: The Vaisala FD70 is a multi-parameter present weather and visibility sensor designed to measure precipitation type, intensity, and visibility with high accuracy in diverse environmental conditions. It uses a combination of forward-scatter measurement and optical disdrometer technologies to detect drop size, fall speeds, and optical properties, enabling the classification of various precipitation types such as rain, snow, sleet, and freezing rain along is visibility estimates. The FD70 provides quantitative estimates of liquid-equivalent precipitation rate and meteorological optical range (MOR), supporting applications in meteorological research, aviation, and road weather monitoring. These measurements are collected at the Argonne Testbed for Multiscale Observational Science (ATMOS), a 20 acre prairie site at Argonne National Lab, located in Lemont, IL. Data is available in netcdf format. Each file contains one second interval data, for approximately 24 hrs each day. File naming convention includes the project (CROCUS), location (ATMOS), instrument name, data level (raw, a1), and date (year, month, day).

measurementTechnique: The FD70 operates out in the open in the ATMOS field site, clear of visual obstructions. The instrument is queried through a dedicated computer to read the data output stream. Instrument drop outs are frequent and can be caused by the dedicated computer experiencing power outages or updates. The instrument can disconnect too due to power resets at the instrument location or comms cables being damaged. The instrument has an internal memory that can track a rolling accumulation of precipitation even if the control computer is disconnected. Therefore, precipitation totals over missed events can still be estimated.

The FD70 reads out data at a 1 hz interval into a mes8 data format created by Vaisala, which is then saved into a text document. The text document is read into a python script that separates the data into their respective variables and decodes the 4680 meteorological codes into the present weather detected using DOE ACT utility for decoding present weather (https://arm-doe.github.io/ACT/API/generated/act.utils.decode_present_weather.html#act.utils.decode_present_weather).

Different variables do have different sampling rates. The instrument overall reports at one second intervals, with multiple variables outputting calculated averages over 10 minute to one hour time periods.
These variables are:
mor_1_minute = "Visibility, 1-minute Average"
mor_10_minute = "Visibility, 10-minute Average"
present_1min_wx = "Present Weather Instant": description: 1 minute present weather using WMO table 4680
present_15min_wx = "Present Weather 15 min"
present_1hr_wx = "Present Weather 1 hr"
temperature = "Ambient Temperature" ; description = "Temperature measurement updated every 10 seconds"
dewpoint = "Dew Point Temperature" ; description = "Dew Point measurement updated every 10 seconds"
relative_humidity = "Relative Humidity" ; description = "Relative Humidity measurement updated every 10 seconds"

Dropsize distribution is broken down in to 41 bins based on mean drop size diameter
Fall speed is broken down into 26 bins for droplet speed.
